title: Hanukkah: Halakha and History

chapters.title: Introduction and the Core Question of Hanukkah
chapters.about: Hosting thanks, prioritizing mitzvot, and introducing the Gemara's question on Hanukkah.

chapters.title: Three Levels of Understanding Hanukkah
chapters.about: Exploring Hanukkah halachically, historically, and theologically or ideologically.

chapters.title: Historical Background: Alexander the Great and Aristotle
chapters.about: The conquest of Alexander the Great, his connection to Aristotle, and Aristotle's concept of God.

chapters.title: Division of the Empire and Hellenization
chapters.about: Division among Alexander's generals, rule over Palestine, and the spread of Hellenistic culture and schools.

chapters.title: The Septuagint and Alexandria Jewry
chapters.about: Translating the Bible into Greek, the impact on language, and Philo of Alexandria.

chapters.title: Contemporary Analogies and Assimilation
chapters.about: Comparing ancient Hellenization to modern Americanization and responses of different Jewish groups.

chapters.title: Antiochus IV and the Maccabean Revolt
chapters.about: Antiochus IV's decrees, the civil war against the Mityavanim, and the military and political victory of the Makkabim.

chapters.title: The Ideological Message of Hanukkah Today
chapters.about: Pirsum Hanes, combating assimilation, and educating children on Jewish identity.

summary: Rabbi Dr. Ezra Labaton A"H explores the holiday of Hanukkah through historical and ideological perspectives, focusing on the interface between Jewish identity and Hellenistic culture. He contrasts the historical backdrop of Greek rule, the Maccabean revolt, and assimilation with contemporary challenges of Americanization and Jewish continuity.
questions: What is Hanukkah really all about according to the Gemara and tradition?
How did Alexander the Great and Aristotle influence the spread of Hellenistic culture among Jews?
Why was the translation of the Bible into Greek, known as the Septuagint, a turning point for Jewish assimilation?
How does the historical struggle against Hellenization parallel modern cultural assimilation in America?
What is the deeper ideological message behind lighting the Hanukkah menorah and publicizing the miracle?
